Правила работы (они важнее всего остального):
- Начни сразу с правки, а не с чтения. Твой первый шаг — открыть tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el и lib/yeah-bridge.el. Больше ничего сначала не читай: AGENTS.md, docs/PLAN.md, docs/ENGINEERING.md уже прочитаны тобой в предыдущем прогоне, их содержание ты знаешь.
- Не запускай `./scripts/dev run` и не запускай `./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*`: это десять минут, и провайдер рвёт соединение во время долгого ожидания. Проверяй только то, что ты изменил: `./scripts/dev byte-compile-all`, `./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el` и конкретную проверку `./scripts/dev check tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el`.
- Каждый твой ответ — это вызов инструмента, а не описание следующего шага. Если ты описал, что сейчас сделаешь, харнест потратит нудж и напомнит.
- Не читай журналы прошлых прогонов и не ищи историю git: они не нужны для этой задачи.

Дефект: одна проверка моста — гонка. Проверка tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el читает буфер подключённого Emacs сто двадцать раз, пока отдельный поток крутится и делает родителя медленным, и падает только когда ответ действительно потерян. 16 ноября 2026 шесть прогонов доказательства дали пять укусов и один промах: control дошёл до предмета, проверка после control всё равно прошла, claim вышел inconclusive, а карта метода вышла unknown. Код виноват не был — виновато было доказательство.

Что должно измениться: проверка перестаёт гнаться за предметом и начинает им распоряжаться. Потеря ответа становится условием, которое проверка сама создаёт — барьер, который ждёт родитель, или хук, который принадлежит проверке, — так что один и тот же вход даёт один и тот же вердикт каждый раз. Control проверяемого claim'а — та же схема с одним шагом, убранным, и тогда проверка обязана падать на своём же утверждении, а не на краше Emacs и не на таймауте.

Что нужно сделать:
1. Пере-регистрировать claim bridge-keeps-the-answer в spec.json с control'ом, который кусается каждый раз (register: fact, требование: проверка моста).
2. Добавить новый claim the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction: проверка моста даёт один и тот же вердикт на десяти последовательных прогонах control'а, и control кусается на каждом из них.
3. Критерии выхода: десять последовательных прогонов control'а кусаются, каждый падает на утверждении проверки; и проверка, запущенная без control'а, проходит стабильно.

Правила репозитория обязательны: lib/ — только Elisp, одна фича на файл, публичные символы с yeah-, внутренние с yeah--, доменные ошибки — user-error или структурированные ошибки, никакой телеметрии, никаких глобальных дефолтов и глобальных перехватов gptel, подпроцессы через make-process. Проверка моста поднимает настоящий Emacs-демон: emacs и emacsclient лежат в ~/.nix-profile/bin, а в переменной EMACS уже указан этот путь.

Когда работа сделана и проверена, закончи через инструмент finish и вкратце скажи, что изменилось и чем ты это проверил.

;;; yeah-bridge.el --- the emacsclient bridge -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
;; it under the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; An explicit, permissioned bridge to the buffers of an attached
;; Emacs, reached through `emacsclient'.  The bridge is a capability
;; and not a convenience: the two tools carry their own names, so
;; the permission system can approve `bridge__eval' and
;; `bridge__buffer_read' separately, and nothing enters the tool
;; registry until the operator asks for it with `yeah-bridge-register'.
;;
;; The program is started with `make-process' -- never through a
;; shell -- and every call is bounded by a short timeout, so a busy
;; or absent server cannot hang the agent.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-tools)

(defgroup yeah-bridge nil
  "The Yeah emacsclient bridge."
  :group 'yeah)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-program "emacsclient"
  "Program used to reach the attached Emacs.
The program is run directly, without a shell, so it must be an
executable found on `exec-path' or the path of an executable file."
  :type 'string
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defcustom yeah-bridge-server nil
  "Name of the Emacs server the bridge connects to.
When nil, `emacsclient' connects to the default server.  A service
placement reaches a specific attached Emacs, so the name is a
capability: the operator names which Emacs the bridge may reach."
  :type '(choice (const nil) string)
  :group 'yeah-bridge)

(defconst yeah-bridge--timeout 2
  "Seconds a bridge call may take before its process is killed.")

(defconst yeah-bridge--probe "t"
  "Expression evaluated to find out whether the attached Emacs answers.")

(defun yeah-bridge--program-path ()
  "Return the path of the executable bridge program, or nil.
The program is not found when `yeah-bridge-program' is empty or
names a file that cannot be executed."
  (let ((program yeah-bridge-program))
    (and (stringp program)
         (> (length program) 0)
         (executable-find program))))

(defun yeah-bridge--trim (text)
  "Return TEXT without its trailing newlines."
  (let* ((text (or text ""))
         (end (length text)))
    (while (and (> end 0)
                (memq (aref text (1- end)) '(?\n ?\r)))
      (setq end (1- end)))
    (substring text 0 end)))

(defun yeah-bridge--stderr-text (buffer)
  "Return the text collected in the stderr BUFFER."
  (with-current-buffer buffer
    (buffer-string)))

(defun yeah-bridge--wait (process timeout)
  "Wait for PROCESS to exit, but no longer than TIMEOUT seconds.
Return non-nil when the process exited in time."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) timeout)))
    (while (and (process-live-p process)
                (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output process 0.05))
    (not (process-live-p process))))

(defun yeah-bridge--run-program (path args timeout)
  "Run PATH with ARGS and collect what it printed.
Return a plist with the keys `:ok', `:status', `:output' and
`:message'; see `yeah-bridge--run' for their meaning."
  (let ((output "")
        (stderr-buffer (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge stderr*"))
        (process nil))
    (unwind-protect
        (condition-case err
            (progn
              (setq process (make-process
                             :name "yeah-bridge"
                             :command (cons path args)
                             :connection-type 'pipe
                             :noquery t
                             :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                             :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                                       (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                             :stderr stderr-buffer))
              (yeah-bridge--wait process timeout)
              (let ((timed-out (process-live-p process)))
                (when timed-out
                  (ignore-errors (kill-process process)))
                ;; A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
                ;; filter: the answer of the attached Emacs is then lost
                ;; and the bridge answers with nothing.  Draining the
                ;; pending events after the exit — until the output stops
                ;; changing — gives the filter its last words.
                (let ((previous nil)
                      (drain-deadline (+ (float-time) 0.2)))
                  (while (and (< (float-time) drain-deadline)
                              (not (equal previous output)))
                    (setq previous output)
                    (accept-process-output nil 0.05)))
                (let ((status (unless timed-out (process-exit-status process))))
                  (list :ok (and (not timed-out) (eq status 0))
                        :status status
                        :output (yeah-bridge--trim output)
                        :message
                        (cond
                         (timed-out
                          (format "the attached Emacs did not answer within %s seconds"
                                  timeout))
                         ((not (eq status 0))
                          (let ((text (yeah-bridge--trim
                                       (yeah-bridge--stderr-text stderr-buffer))))
                            (if (> (length text) 0)
                                (format "the attached Emacs reported: %s" text)
                              "the attached Emacs reported an error")))
                         (t nil))))))
          (error
           (list :ok nil
                 :status nil
                 :output ""
                 :message (error-message-string err))))
      (when (and process (process-live-p process))
        (ignore-errors (delete-process process)))
      (when (buffer-live-p stderr-buffer)
        (kill-buffer stderr-buffer)))))

(defun yeah-bridge--run (args &optional timeout)
  "Run the bridge program with ARGS and collect what it printed.
ARGS is the list of command-line arguments without the program
itself.  TIMEOUT is the number of seconds the process may run.

Return a plist with the keys `:ok' (non-nil when the program
answered successfully), `:status' (the exit status), `:output' (the
standard output without trailing newlines) and `:message' (why the
call failed, or nil)."
  (let ((path (yeah-bridge--program-path))
        (args (append (when (and (stringp yeah-bridge-server)
                                 (> (length yeah-bridge-server) 0))
                        (list "-s" yeah-bridge-server))
                      args)))
    (if (null path)
        (list :ok nil
              :status nil
              :output ""
              :message (format "the bridge program %S is not executable"
                               yeah-bridge-program))
      (yeah-bridge--run-program path args (or timeout yeah-bridge--timeout)))))

(defun yeah-bridge-available-p ()
  "Return non-nil when the attached Emacs answers the bridge program.
The program must be executable and the attached Emacs must reply
within the bridge timeout.  This never signals: any failure means
that the bridge is unavailable."
  (condition-case nil
      (let ((result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" yeah-bridge--probe))))
        (and (plist-get result :ok)
             (> (length (or (plist-get result :output) "")) 0)))
    (error nil)))

(defun yeah-bridge-eval (expression)
  "Evaluate EXPRESSION in the attached Emacs and return the printed result.
EXPRESSION is a string of Elisp code.  The result is the printed
value, as a string, without trailing newlines.

Signals `user-error' when the bridge is unavailable and when the
evaluation itself fails; the message says which of the two happened."
  (unless (stringp expression)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-bridge-eval: expression must be a string, got %S"
                          (type-of expression)))))
  (let ((result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" expression))))
    (if (plist-get result :ok)
        (plist-get result :output)
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-bridge-eval: %s"
                            (if (yeah-bridge-available-p)
                                (format "evaluation failed: %s"
                                        (or (plist-get result :message)
                                            "unknown error"))
                              "the bridge is unavailable")))))))

(defun yeah-bridge--decode (output)
  "Return the string OUTPUT holds, decoding its printed form.
`emacsclient --eval' prints the value of the evaluation: a string
arrives quoted, as its printed form.  When OUTPUT looks like a printed
string it is read back; anything else is returned unchanged."
  (if (and (stringp output)
           (> (length output) 1)
           (eq (aref output 0) ?\"))
      (condition-case nil (read output) (error output))
    output))

(defun yeah-bridge-buffer-read (name)
  "Return the text of the live buffer NAME of the attached Emacs.
NAME is the name of a buffer in the attached Emacs.  The result is
its text, as a string, without trailing newlines.

Signals `user-error' when the bridge is unavailable and when the
buffer cannot be read there; the message says which of the two
happened."
  (unless (stringp name)
    (signal 'user-error
            (list (format "yeah-bridge-buffer-read: name must be a string, got %S"
                          (type-of name)))))
  (let* ((expression
          (format (concat "(with-current-buffer %S "
                          "(buffer-substring-no-properties (point-min) (point-max)))")
                  name))
         (result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" expression))))
    (if (plist-get result :ok)
        (yeah-bridge--decode (plist-get result :output))
      (signal 'user-error
              (list (format "yeah-bridge-buffer-read: %s"
                            (if (yeah-bridge-available-p)
                                (format "buffer %S could not be read: %s"
                                        name
                                        (or (plist-get result :message)
                                            "unknown error"))
                              "the bridge is unavailable")))))))

(defun yeah-bridge-tool-specs ()
  "Return the bridge tool specifications, in registration order."
  (list
   (list :name "bridge__eval"
         :description
         "Evaluate an Elisp expression in the attached Emacs and return the printed value."
         :input (list (list :name "expression" :type 'string))
         :handler #'yeah-bridge-eval)
   (list :name "bridge__buffer_read"
         :description
         "Return the contents of a live buffer of the attached Emacs."
         :input (list (list :name "name" :type 'string))
         :handler #'yeah-bridge-buffer-read)))

(defun yeah-bridge-register ()
  "Register the bridge tools in the tool registry and return them.
The registration is idempotent: a tool that is already registered is
kept as it is, so calling this twice does not raise an error.
The permission system matches the tool name as the action, so
`\"bridge__eval\"' and `\"bridge__buffer_read\"' are approved on
their own."
  (let ((specs (yeah-bridge-tool-specs)))
    (dolist (spec specs)
      (unless (yeah-tools-get (plist-get spec :name))
        (yeah-tools-register spec)))
    specs))

(provide 'yeah-bridge)
;;; yeah-bridge.el ends here

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el --- the bridge does not lose the answer -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the filter:
;; the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success with an empty
;; output — the person saw an empty buffer that the server had never
;; emptied.  This check reads the same live buffer many times through the
;; bridge and requires that no answer is ever empty.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--reads 120
  "How many times the check reads the buffer through the bridge.
Losing an answer is a race between the exit of the child process and the
delivery of its last chunk, so it shows up under load: the check keeps a
thread spinning to make the parent late, and reads often enough that the
loss is certain without the fix.")

(defvar yeah-check--load-thread nil
  "The thread that keeps the parent late, so the race can happen.")

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000)))
      (empty 0))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (make-process
         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
                        "--eval"
                        "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") (insert \"live text\"))")
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)
        ;; wait for the server
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
                                                  "-s" name "--eval" "t")))))
            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
        ;; a spinning thread makes the parent slow, which is when the
        ;; answer of the child is lost
        (setq yeah-check--load-thread
              (make-thread
               (lambda ()
                 (let ((counter 0))
                   (while (< counter 100000000)
                     (setq counter (1+ counter)))))))
        (dotimes (_ yeah-check--reads)
          (let ((text (condition-case err
                         (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                               (yeah-bridge-server name))
                           (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                       (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
            (when (or (null text) (equal text ""))
              (setq empty (1+ empty)))))
        (when (> empty 0)
          (push (format "the bridge lost the answer %d times out of %d"
                        empty yeah-check--reads)
                failures)))
    (when yeah-check--load-thread
      (ignore-errors (thread-signal yeah-check--load-thread 'quit)))
    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)"))))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el ends here

barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same

the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.

**The estimate.**  One to two days, and a key of the provider for the live
part.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The budget of the completion
supervision of a child is zero today, and that is a decision of the owner
(§17.2), not a defect of this wave.

### 18.5 What this plan does not decide

Three decisions of the owner stay open, and no wave above takes them:
- the threshold of the parity, and the final set of the tasks of the benchmark
  (`docs/PLAN.md` §13): until it is decided, the parity is not claimed
  anywhere, and the pilot stays a measurement;
- whether a run that the provider silenced is a failure of the agent or a run
  that was never measured: it changes the number of every pilot;
- the budget of the completion supervision of a child of a delegation: the
  default of the kernel is positive since wave 39, the default of the child is
  still zero.

Two more items of the open work (§17.1) are not in the order above and stay
where they are: the pilot again, with a larger set of tasks, when the
provider answers; and the pixel check, which waits for the owner to name the
place of the frame server.

irement: the check of the\n  bridge).\n- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the\n  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the\n  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).\n\n**The exit criteria.**\n1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an\n   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.\n2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`\n   claim and no `unknown` verdict.\n\n**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It\nrepairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.\n\n### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin\n\n**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP\nserver outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open\nafter the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.\nAnd some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:\none of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six\nvoluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.\n\n**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the\ncause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,\nand a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four\nper cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of\nthe provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`\nare not available in this environment (\"Operation not permitted\"), so the\nlocalization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,\nnot the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.\n\n**What changes.**\n1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the\n   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The\n   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe\n   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives\n   it a way to say so.\n2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by\n   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the\n   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.\n   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.\n\n**The claims.**\n- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is\n  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open\n  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must\n  fail).\n- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose\n  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten\n  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must\n  exceed the bound).\n\n**The exit criteria.**\n1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.\n2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive\n   measurements.\n3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.\n\n**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A\ntransport that dies with \"Curl failed with exit code 28\" is the provider's\ndeath, not the harness's.\n\n### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs\n\n**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,\nand all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent\nwhere the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what\nthe agent did.\n\n1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is\n   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools\n   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of\n   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live\n   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of\n   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.\n2. The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a\n   session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is\n   answered with `-32601`.\n3. The owner named the order of the next waves on 2026-11-16 (az), after the

opens the path from a model to a working program goes last.

process of the server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave
44 (parallel children in a live turn).

One wave was executed before them: **wave 45** (2026-11-17), the repair of
the harness that the live test of the harness forced — a tool that returns
bytes that are not text took the whole Emacs process down, and the four
waves of this plan need a harness that lives to carry them (§16.24).  The

four.

control that has to bite, and the criteria that close it.  A wave that ends
without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,

  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must

   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

now_ms() {
  printf '%s' "$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))"
}

case "$cmd" in
  help|--help|-h)
    cat <<'EOF'
scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper

Subcommands:

  byte-compile-all      — byte-compile lib/*.el (including lib/yeah.el), no warnings

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el --- the bridge does not lose the answer -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the filter:
;; the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success with an empty
;; output — the person saw an empty buffer that the server had never
;; emptied.  This check reads the same live buffer many times through the
;; bridge and requires that no answer is ever empty.

;;; Code:

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv "EMACS") (file-executable-p (getenv "EMACS"))
           (getenv "EMACS"))
      (executable-find "emacs")
      (expand-file-name "~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"))
  "The Emacs program that runs the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name "emacsclient" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find "emacsclient")
        candidate))
  "The emacsclient program that reaches the server.")

(defvar yeah-check--reads 120
  "How many times the check reads the buffer through the bridge.
Losing an answer is a race between the exit of the child process and the
delivery of its last chunk, so it shows up under load: the check keeps a
thread spinning to make the parent late, and reads often enough that the
loss is certain without the fix.")

(defvar yeah-check--load-thread nil
  "The thread that keeps the parent late, so the race can happen.")

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format "yeah-bridge-keep-%d" (random 1000000)))
      (empty 0))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (make-process
         :name "yeah-bridge-keep-server"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat "--daemon=" name)
                        "--eval"
                        "(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \"*yeah-live*\") (insert \"live text\"))")
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)
        ;; wait for the server
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
                                                  "-s" name "--eval" "t")))))
            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
        ;; a spinning thread makes the parent slow, which is when the
        ;; answer of the child is lost
        (setq yeah-check--load-thread
              (make-thread
               (lambda ()
                 (let ((counter 0))
                   (while (< counter 100000000)
                     (setq counter (1+ counter)))))))
        (dotimes (_ yeah-check--reads)
          (let ((text (condition-case err
                         (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                               (yeah-bridge-server name))
                           (yeah-bridge-buffer-read "*yeah-live*"))
                       (error (format "ERROR: %S" err)))))
            (when (or (null text) (equal text ""))
              (setq empty (1+ empty)))))
        (when (> empty 0)
          (push (format "the bridge lost the answer %d times out of %d"
                        empty yeah-check--reads)
                failures)))
    (when yeah-check--load-thread
      (ignore-errors (thread-signal yeah-check--load-thread 'quit)))
    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil "-s" name "--eval" "(kill-emacs)"))))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message "bridge-keep: %s" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el ends here

**The product.**

- A real editor (an agent-shell, or a person's Emacs) against a live provider:
  not yet checked.  The ACP agent and the MCP server are driven by a
  third-party client with a fake model, and the service path itself is
  verified with a live provider.
- The service path has no mode changes of the attached path and no opening of
  an earlier session by name.
- The bridge to the buffers of an attached Emacs is verified against a live
  Emacs server (a real daemon), and not against a person's Emacs in day-to-day
  use.
- The stdio server answers one request at a time: a cancel that arrives while
  a prompt is running is read after that prompt reaches a terminal state.  The
  socket transport does not have this limit.
- The picture of the interface is compared with itself and with the same
  buffer without the interface, and not with a stored golden picture.
- PTC stays an experimental, off-by-default restricted evaluator, and not a
  security boundary.

**The ACP surface, as an orchestrator sees it.**  The gaps below were found by
the integration with Paseo (docs/PASEO-INTEGRATION.md) and are still open.

- The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is recorded
  in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools do not read
  it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the working directory of the
  Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  An orchestrator
  that asks for a run in a repository gets a run in the directory of the
  service.
- The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
  session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is answered
  with `-32601`.
- The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
  `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists, so an
  orchestrator cannot choose the model of a run.
- The `mcpServers` of a session are ignored: the tools of an MCP server that a
  client names do not reach the model.
- The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
  with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`), but no `kind`: a
  client that renders the call of a tool by its kind — a read, an edit, a
  shell — sees the name of the tool and nothing else.  The arguments of a
  call are positional, so a client that looks for named fields (`path`,
  `oldText`, `query`) does not find them.
- The process of the server outlives the agent.  A client that keeps the pipe
  of the server open after the last turn leaves an Emacs process alive, and
  some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace: one

without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

**The claims.**
- `the-server-exits-when-the-session-is-over` — the process of the server is
  gone after the session ends, even when the client keeps the pipe open
  (the control keeps the pipe open and ends the session: the check must
  fail).
- `the-server-does-not-spin-when-the-provider-is-silent` — a server whose
  provider went silent costs less than one per cent of a core over ten
  seconds (the control brings the busy loop back: the measured ticks must
  exceed the bound).

**The exit criteria.**
1. A server left behind by a finished session is gone within ten seconds.
2. The ticks of a silent server stay under the bound in ten consecutive
   measurements.
3. The live check of the plugin leaves no process behind.

**The estimate.**  One to two days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  A
transport that dies with "Curl failed with exit code 28" is the provider's
death, not the harness's.

### 18.3 Wave 43 — the surface of ACP that an orchestrator needs

**The defect.**  The integration with Paseo found four gaps of the surface,
and all of them point the same way: an orchestrator cannot put the agent
where the work is, cannot change what the agent may do, and cannot read what
the agent did.

1. The working directory of a session — the `cwd` of `session/new` — is
   recorded in the journal and in the frozen input of the run, but the tools
   do not read it: a relative path of a tool is counted from the directory of
   the Emacs process and not from the directory of the session.  In the live
   check the `bash` of the agent ran in the directory of the installation of
   the CLI of Paseo, not in the repository of the task.
2. The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
   session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is
   answered with `-32601`.
3. The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
   `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists.
4. The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
   with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`, since wave 40), but
   no `kind`: a client that renders the call of a tool by its kind — a read,
   an edit, a shell — sees the name of the tool and nothing else.  The
   arguments of a call are positional, so a client that looks for named
   fields (`path`, `oldText`, `query`) does not find them.

**What changes.**  The gaps are closed in the order of what the live
integration needs today: the `cwd` first, because the agent must work in the
repository of the task; then the `kind` of the call and its named arguments,
because the client must be able to show what the agent did; then
`session/set_mode`; then the model of the session; then the `mcpServers` of
the session, whose tools do not reach the model today.

**The claims.**  Each gap is a claim of its own, and the name of the claim is
the name of the gap: `a-session-runs-in-its-own-directory`,
`a-tool-call-carries-its-kind`, `a-tool-call-carries-named-arguments`,
`a-session-changes-its-permission-profile-over-the-wire`,
`a-session-changes-its-model-over-the-wire`,
`the-mcp-servers-of-a-session-reach-the-model`.

**The exit criteria.**
1. The check of the `cwd` sends a session into a temporary directory, and the
   tool of that session sees the temporary directory and not the directory of
   the process.
2. The plugin of Paseo runs a turn in the repository of the task, and the
   timeline of the client shows the kind of the call of the tool.
3. The wire answers `session/set_mode` and no longer answers `-32601`.

**The estimate.**  Two to three days.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The
wire of Yeah is ACP plus the one extension that was announced
(`yeah.queueEvents`); this wave adds no method that ACP does not have.

### 18.4 Wave 44 — parallel children in a live turn

**The defect.**  Several children in one turn of the parent work already: the
audit of wave 35 proved it, and the plan that said otherwise was wrong.  What
is not proven is a *live* turn of a parent with two children of a live
provider.  No child of a live provider has run on a model other than the
model of its parent, and the live checks do not exercise the delegation at
all: the benchmark gives its runs a fixed set of tools, and the delegation is
not among them.

**What changes.**  The live check grows a second child in the same turn of
the parent, and the offline check with a fake model becomes the claim that
the map binds — the live check lives outside the map, because it needs a
provider.

**The claims.**
- `two-children-run-in-one-turn-of-the-parent` — the claim of the map, with a
  fake model: two delegations in one turn of the parent give two children,
  both alive, and the turn of the parent goes on (the control refuses the
  second delegation: the check must fail).
- `a-child-runs-on-the-model-of-its-preset` — the model of a child is the
  model of the preset, and not the model of its parent (the control names
  another model in the preset: the child must run on it).

**The exit criteria.**
1. The offline check passes and its control bites.
2. The live check with a real provider shows two children in one turn of the
   parent, and the tree of the children in the journal holds both.

**The estimate.**  One to two days, and a key of the provider for the live
part.  **What this wave does not fix.**  The budget of the completion
supervision of a child is zero today, and that is a decision of the owner
(§17.2), not a defect of this wave.

### 18.5 What this plan does not decide

Three decisions of the owner stay open, and no wave above takes them:
- the threshold of the parity, and the final set of the tasks of the benchmark

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

  "The Yeah emacsclient bridge."
  :group 'yeah)

  "Program used to reach the attached Emacs.

executable found on `exec-path' or the path of an executable file."

placement reaches a specific attached Emacs, so the name is a
capability: the operator names which Emacs the bridge may reach."

  :group 'yeah-bridge)

  "Seconds a bridge call may take before its process is killed.")

  "Return the path of the executable bridge program, or nil.

names a file that cannot be executed."
  (let ((program yeah-bridge-program))
    (and (stringp program)
         (> (length program) 0)
         (executable-find program))))

  "Return TEXT without its trailing newlines."
  (let* ((text (or text ""))
         (end (length text)))
    (while (and (> end 0)
                (memq (aref text (1- end)) '(?\n ?\r)))
      (setq end (1- end)))
    (substring text 0 end)))

  "Return the text collected in the stderr BUFFER."
  (with-current-buffer buffer
    (buffer-string)))

  "Wait for PROCESS to exit, but no longer than TIMEOUT seconds.
Return non-nil when the process exited in time."
  (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) timeout)))
    (while (and (process-live-p process)
                (< (float-time) deadline))
      (accept-process-output process 0.05))
    (not (process-live-p process))))

  "Run PATH with ARGS and collect what it printed.

`:message'; see `yeah-bridge--run' for their meaning."
  (let ((output "")
        (stderr-buffer (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge stderr*"))
        (process nil))
    (unwind-protect
        (condition-case err
            (progn
              (setq process (make-process
                             :name "yeah-bridge"
                             :command (cons path args)
                             :connection-type 'pipe
                             :noquery t
                             :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                             :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                                       (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                             :stderr stderr-buffer))
              (yeah-bridge--wait process timeout)
              (let ((timed-out (process-live-p process)))
                (when timed-out
                  (ignore-errors (kill-process process)))
                ;; A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the

                (let ((status (unless timed-out (process-exit-status process))))

                        :status status
                        :output (yeah-bridge--trim output)
                        :message
                        (cond
                         (timed-out
                          (format "the attached Emacs did not answer within %s seconds"
                                  timeout))
                         ((not (eq status 0))
                          (let ((text (yeah-bridge--trim
                                       (yeah-bridge--stderr-text stderr-buffer))))

                         (t nil))))))

itself.  TIMEOUT is the number of seconds the process may run.

answered successfully), `:status' (the exit status), `:output' (the

call failed, or nil)."

        (args (append (when (and (stringp yeah-bridge-server)
                                 (> (length yeah-bridge-server) 0))
                        (list "-s" yeah-bridge-server))
                      args)))
    (if (null path)
        (list :ok nil
              :status nil

      (let ((result (yeah-bridge--run (list "--eval" yeah-bridge--probe))))

(defun yeah-bridge-eval (expression)

---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

now_ms() {
  printf '%s' "$(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))"
}

case "$cmd" in
  help|--help|-h)
    cat <<'EOF'
scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper

Subcommands:
  smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
  byte-compile-all      — byte-compile lib/*.el (including lib/yeah.el), no warnings
  ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
  bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
  pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
  map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
  run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
  gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
  help                  — this text

Exit codes:
  0 — pass       (Green)
  1 — fail       (Red)
  2 — blocked    (input error)
  3 — unknown    (the method could not tell)

Environment:
  MATHC  — path to the math-coding binary (default: `mathc` on PATH)
  EMACS  — path to the Emacs binary (default: `emacs` on PATH)
EOF
    ;;

  smoke)
    echo "yeah-dev ok ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))"
    exit 0
    ;;

  byte-compile-all)
    emacs_bin="$(find_emacs)" || {
      echo "scripts/dev byte-compile-all: emacs is not on PATH and EMACS is not set" >&2

# AGENTS.md — the entry point to this repository

> **Yeah** means **Yeah, Emacs Agent Harness**: a recursive acronym, the
> **Y** is the Y-combinator. The harness itself is
> Emacs Lisp; Emacs is not merely a client to an external agent. The model is
> reached through gptel, effects go through the tool registry and permission
> system, and session history is append-only JSONL.
>
> The long-term Y metaphor means bounded recursive delegation, runtime
> self-inspection and a fixed point where Yeah can develop and verify Yeah.
> These are goals, not assertions about today's prototype.
>
> This repository is governed by **math-coding v5**: `spec.json` holds the
> standing specification (`schema_version: 5`) and the claims, `waves/*.json`
> holds the historical work units, and evidence comes from checks bound by
> `mathc run`.  Version 4 is frozen and archived at `waves/spec-v4.json`;
> its evidence is not current.
> `docs/PLAN.md` defines the current target sequence; do not mistake an old
> wave number or a green module row for a working end-to-end feature.

## Read first, in this order

1. `README.md` — actual current status and explicit limitations.
2. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the normative target: purpose, ten decisions,
   contracts, security, placements and non-goals.
3. `docs/PLAN.md` — the detailed eight-stage execution plan and release gates.
4. `docs/ENGINEERING.md` — binding dependency, infrastructure, library,
   process, security, testing and packaging practices.
5. `spec.json` — the standing machine-checked specification.
6. `waves/*.json` — existing math-coding units, with intent, check, promise
   and objection.
7. `ELISP_BEST_PRACTICES.md` — kernel Elisp conventions; §11 is the trap log.
8. `lib/yeah-*.el` — the implementation, one feature per file.

If two sources contradict each other, report the contradiction in the open
work item. Never resolve it by silently making documentation more optimistic.

## Current warnings for every agent

- This is a kernel prototype, not a usable coding product.
- The parity with other harnesses was piloted on 2026-11-15, and the
  difference the pilot found was a defect of the turn, not a difference of
  quality: after the results of the tool calls arrive, the model may answer
  with an empty message, and the turn took that as the end of the work and
  stopped without the effect (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot of the
  parity").  The defect is fixed (the claim
  `an-empty-answer-does-not-end-the-run'), and the pilot on the fixed turn
  moved one task of three; the nudge now carries the state of the work
  (the claim `a-silence-nudge-carries-the-state-of-the-work'), because the
  provider goes silent after every batch of tool results and the model was
  answering the nudge by starting the work over.  With that, Yeah passes
  two tasks of three and pi passes three.  The third task failed in the
  tools: the `read` of a file nobody has edited yet returns no tick, and
  the `edit` refused the tick the model guessed as stale although the file
  has not changed; wave 26 makes a guessed tick ignored rather than
  refused (the claim
  `a-guessed-tick-does-not-refuse-an-unchanged-file'), and that task of the
  pilot passes now.  The provider was overloaded for hours (HTTP 529 to both
  harnesses), so the pilot of 15:02 measured one task of three and two
  blocked runs: the runner records a run the provider stopped as **blocked**,
  neither a pass nor a failure (the claim
  `a-provider-failure-is-not-a-failure-of-the-agent').  The pilot of 15:39, on
  the code of wave 28, measured two tasks of three — Yeah passed both of them
  and pi passed all three — and the third was blocked, because the transport
  to the provider died.  The parity of that run is not measured either.  The
  pilot of 17:06, on the code of waves 30+31, measured one task of three for
  Yeah and two of three for pi: all three runs of Yeah ended `unfinished`,
  because the provider goes silent, and the one task that failed in the tools
  failed on the **version token** of the file — the model copied 58 of the 64
  characters of the digest and the edit refused the edit of a file that had
  not changed (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot that measured the copy of the
  version token").  The pilot of 17:23, on the code of wave 32, measured two
  tasks of three for Yeah and three of three for pi: the token of the file is
  short now, the read handed out twelve characters, and the tasks the model
  worked on passed.  The task that Yeah failed failed on the provider: the
  model announced the fix ("Fixing it to use floating-point division:") and
  called no tool (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The pilot after the token became
  short").  The pilot of 2026-11-16 06:43–06:48, on the code of wave 33, measured
  two tasks of three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the pilot of
  07:04, on the code of wave 34, measured one task of three for Yeah and three
  of three for pi.  Both failures were the same failure of the model and not of
  the harness: the model read the files of the task and never called the tool
  that would change them, while the guards of waves 29, 32, 33 and 34 were
  never in the way (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the pilot after
  wave 34").  The pilot of 08:07, on the code of wave 35, measured two tasks of
  three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the third task of Yeah was
  blocked: the transport to the provider died with "Curl failed with exit code
  28" after the model had read the file and computed the sum.  A run that the
  provider stops is blocked and not a failure of the agent, and it says
  nothing about either harness (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the
  pilot after wave 35").  The pilot of 10:00, on the code of wave 36, measured
  two tasks of three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the third task of
  Yeah failed in the tools: the model read the file, computed the sum with
  `bash` (the tool answered 100) and then answered with an empty message three
  times; the harness nudged three times, every nudge carrying the state of the
  work, and the run ended "unfinished" with the nudge budget spent.  The file
  was never written, so the runner recorded a failure of the agent; that is
  the shape the provider has had for two days, and `write-new-file` passed in
  the same pilot, so the write path of the code of wave 36 works (docs/
  LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the pilot after wave 36").  The
  pilot of 10:44, on the code of wave 37, measured the same: two tasks of
  three for Yeah and three of three for pi, and the third task of Yeah
  failed in the tools the same way — the model read the file, ran `bash`,
  and then answered with an empty message; the harness nudged it with the
  state of the work, and the model went silent again (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md,
  "The live checks and the pilot after wave 37").  The pilot of 13:12, on the
  code of wave 38, measured one task of three for Yeah and three of three for
  pi: two tasks of Yeah failed in the same shape — the model read the files,
  and then answered with an empty message three times, and the run ended
  "unfinished" with the nudge budget spent.  The row of such a run names the
  shape of it since wave 38, so the reader of the pilot sees the cause of the
  failed check and not only its verdict; the verdict of the row is still the
  verdict, because the classification of a run that did not finish is a
  decision of the owner (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live checks and the
  pilot after wave 38").  The threshold of the
  parity is a decision of the owner (docs/PLAN.md §13), and nobody may quote
  the pilot as a verdict about parity.
- A decision that arrives while the tools of the previous decision are still
  running no longer breaks the run: the turn keeps the calls, runs them when
  the running batch has settled, and gives the model the results of every
  batch together (wave 28, the claims
  `a-decision-that-arrives-while-the-tools-run-does-not-break-the-run' and
  `the-same-tool-call-does-not-run-twice').  The live checks of 15:38 hold
  no transition error at all.  The live coding task still fails, and it fails
  for another reason: the model of the provider answers with an empty message
  and the run ends with the record "unfinished" — the work is not done, and
  the run says so.
- The read of a file shows the file on disk, but the tick it hands out

  read that handed it out (the claim

  optional, so a model that presents no version writes without that guard.

  write goes to the disk and the buffer becomes stale — that is open in
  docs/PLAN-NEXT.md.
- The harness opens the files of the project on behalf of the model, and
  Emacs runs the local variables of a file and the directory-local variables

  and the project is untrusted input: a `mode:` entry names a function that

;;     for them, and then the registry call returns the live text.
;;

;; answer -- probe, evaluate, read a buffer.  Nothing the bridge does
;; today needs a persistent connection; one would matter for streaming
;; the live state of a buffer, which the bridge does not do.

(require 'cl-lib)
(require 'yeah-bridge)
(require 'yeah-tools)

        candidate))

(defun yeah-check--daemon-start (name form)

(defun yeah-check--daemon-eval (name expression)

      (list code (string-trim (buffer-string))))))

(defun yeah-check--daemon-alive-p (name)
  "Return non-nil when the server NAME answers the probe."
  (and (zerop (car (yeah-check--daemon-eval name "t"))) t))

(defun yeah-check--daemon-await (name)
  "Wait until the server NAME answers, at most 8 seconds."

(defun yeah-check--daemon-stop (name)
  "Ask the server NAME to stop."
  (ignore-errors (yeah-check--daemon-eval name "(kill-emacs)")))

(defun yeah-check--bridge-read-until (name expected &optional timeout)
  "Read *yeah-live* of server NAME through the bridge until the text is
EXPECTED, retrying within TIMEOUT seconds (default 15).
A bridge call is killed after the bridge's own 2-second timeout, and on a
loaded machine a single call can lose that race; the check asks for live
state, not for one fast call, so it retries instead of reporting a slow
server as a broken bridge."

- Wave 45 made the harness live.  The live test of Yeah against a real
  provider found four defects that no offline check had seen, because every
  offline check had been written by the same hand as the code.  A `bash'
  tool whose output ends in a byte that is not valid UTF-8 killed the whole
  Emacs process: the refusal of JSON arrived inside the sentinel of the
  process, where no handler of the turn stands, and the run left no record
  of itself (exit code 255).  The bytes arrive in two shapes, and both are
  now text: a unibyte string of bytes, and a multibyte string that holds a
  raw byte where the decoder of a process refused one (a character whose
  code is at or above #x3FFF00).  The text of the harness is decided in one
  place (`lib/yeah-text.el'), and a byte that is not text becomes the
  replacement character (the claim
  `the-text-of-the-harness-is-always-text').  The journal never refuses a
  record: a record that JSON cannot write is written as a stand-in that
  says so, and the journal takes the records that follow (the claim
  `the-journal-never-refuses-a-record').  An error of the harness that
  happens inside the callback of an asynchronous tool becomes a failed tool
  and not the death of the process.  A run whose summary the provider did
  not write does not die either: the old outputs of the tools are pruned,
  the journal says that the summary did not arrive, and the run goes on (the
  claim `a-run-degrades-when-the-summary-does-not-arrive').  The reason of
  a failure that goes into the journal is cut at two thousand characters,
  because a provider that refuses a request hands the whole conversation of
  the run back inside the refusal, and one record of the journal is a
  record and not a transcript (the claim
  `the-record-of-a-failure-is-bounded'; the record of the failure of the
  second live run was 2.8 MB).  The end-to-end check of the first defect
  runs a real child process that runs the real tool
  (tests/checks/check-a-tool-that-returns-bytes-does-not-kill-the-harness.el),
  and all five controls were run and bit; docs/PLAN.md §16.24.  The repaired
  harness was then run against a real provider with a real coding task: the
  model wrote a calculator (5 553 bytes), wrote its own tests (4 699 bytes,
  fifteen where the task asked for eight), ran them and the run of the tests
  outside the harness says `OK` (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The live coding run
  after wave 45").  The same run is the first live proof of the repair: one
  command of the model cut a multibyte character of the journal in half, and
  the journal of the run is valid UTF-8 from the first byte to the last.
  The wave is
  numbered 45 and not 41: the waves 41 to 44 are the plan the owner named
  on 2026-11-16 (docs/PLAN.md §18), and that plan is not rewritten here.
- Wave 46 made the noise of the provider harmless to a run that works.  The
  first live run of Yeah on the task of the owner (the wave 41) called
  seventeen tools and still ended in the state `failed`: the provider answered
  every batch of the results with an empty message, the harness read that
  silence as the silence of a model that does not act, and the budget of the
  nudges was spent on the noise.  The record of that run said "the model
  answered with an empty message 8 times and the run ended without an effect",
  and both halves of it were false: the run had an effect and the model had
  acted.  The budget of the nudges now pays for the nudges that no effect
  answered, and a nudge that follows the silence of the provider after the
  tools of the model have come back does not spend it (the claim
  `the-noise-of-the-provider-does-not-end-a-working-run').  A model that never
  acts still ends, and the record of a run that did not finish names the tools
  the run called, so a run that called its tools is never described as a run
  that ended without an effect (the claim
  `the-record-of-a-run-that-did-not-finish-is-true').  The check of the wave
  plays the shape of that live run with a fake transport, and both of its
  controls were run and bit; docs/PLAN.md §16.25, docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The
  self-development run that found the noise of the provider".
- Wave 47 gave the model the memory of the run.  Every request of the harness
  started a fresh conversation with the model: the prompt was all the model was
  told, so a model that answered with a plan instead of an action began the
  task over.  Two live runs of the wave 41 measured the shape — 108 and 122
  calls of tools, no change of the repository, `AGENTS.md' read ten and nine
  times, the input of the requests not growing at all (4149 tokens at the
  start of the run and 919 after 122 calls).  Every request now carries the
  transcript of the run before the prompt: the call the model made, the result
  it got and the answer it gave, and the words that keep the work where it is
  (the claim `the-model-is-told-what-the-run-has-done').  The transcript is a
  projection of the journal and not a second copy of the run — the journal
  keeps the plain message it was written with (the claim
  `the-transcript-is-a-projection-and-not-a-second-copy-of-the-run').  The
  check of the wave plays the shape of those live runs with a fake transport,
  and both of its controls were run and bit; docs/PLAN.md §16.26,
  docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The self-development runs that found the missing
  memory".
- Wave 48 made the death of the transport harmless to a run that works.  Three
  live runs of the wave 41 died the same way — `Curl failed with exit code 28',
  `16' and `28' — after 108, 122 and 70 calls of tools, and the harness read
  the death of the transport as the end of the run and threw the work of the
  model away with it.  A request that the provider dropped (no HTTP status) and
  a request that met a busy provider (429, 5xx, 529) are asked again, with the
  transcript of the run in front of the model, and the retry is bounded by a
  budget of its own; the journal holds the retry as a record of its own
  (`retry'), and the machine of the states does not move (the claims
  `a-dropped-request-is-asked-again' and `the-retries-of-a-run-are-bounded').
  A request that the provider refused is an answer and is not asked again (the
  claim `a-refused-request-is-not-asked-again').  The status of the wire
  decides which of the two it is, and gptel reports it as a string, so it is
  read as a number: without that a refusal of the provider would have been
  taken for a request that was never answered.  The check of the wave plays
  the shape of those live runs with a fake provider, down to the string that
  carries the status, and all three of its controls were run and bit; docs/PLAN.md
  §16.27, docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The run on the code of wave 47 and the death
  of the transport".
- The working directory of a session (`cwd') is still not applied to the
  tools: in the live check the `bash' of the agent ran in the directory of
  the process, not in the repository of the task (docs/PLAN.md §17.1).
- The live stand of the transport was at fault, and not the provider: it stopped
  waiting at the first line that arrived, and the empty string that a
  reasoning model sends between its thinking and its answer was the absence of
  an answer.  The decision what counts as an answer now lives in
  tests/support/yeah-live-answer.el and is tested offline — text with content
  and a tool call are answers, the empty string, the streaming sentinel and the
  reasoning are not (the claim `the-live-stand-waits-for-an-answer').
- Stage 6 is implemented offline: the run context owns the session, the
  transport, the answerer and the rules of one run, and the three
  placements — attached, service, batch — write the same events for the

- Stage 5 is implemented offline: the ACP agent and the MCP server speak

  now driven by a third-party client (xenodium/acp.el) with a fake model;

  tests/live/live-service-path.el;

{
  "id": "wave-48",
  "title": "a request the provider dropped is asked again, and a request the provider refused is not",
  "intent": "Three live runs of the wave 41 died the same way and for the same reason: the run of 2026-11-17 16:15 with `Curl failed with exit code 28' after 108 calls of tools, the run of 16:26 with `Curl failed with exit code 16' after 122 calls of tools, and the run of 17:10 with `Curl failed with exit code 28' after 70 calls of tools.  The transport to the provider died, the harness took the death of the transport for the end of the run, and the work of the model — hundreds of calls of tools, a plan read over and over — was thrown away with it.  The request never reached an answer: a provider that drops the connection did not refuse the request, and the run said nothing about that difference.  The wave asks such a request again.  The retry is bounded by a budget of its own (`yeah-turn-default-max-retries'), the journal holds the retry as a record of its own (`retry'), and the model is asked the same question with what the run has done in front of it (wave 47), so the retry continues the work instead of starting it over.  A request that the provider refused is not asked again: a refusal is an answer, and the run fails at once and says why.  The status of the wire decides which of the two it is, and the transport of gptel reports that status as a string (`\"529\"', `\"400\"'), so the status is read as a number and not only as a number.  The wave was found by live runs and not by an offline check, and the check that covers it plays the shape of those runs with a fake provider: no network is touched, but the shape is the one that broke the harness, down to the string that carries the status.",

    "lib/yeah-turn.el",
    "lib/yeah-events.el",

    "./scripts/dev check tests/checks/check-a-dropped-request-is-asked-again.el",
    "./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*"

  "claims": [
    "a-dropped-request-is-asked-again",
    "a-refused-request-is-not-asked-again",
    "the-retries-of-a-run-are-bounded"

  "commitment": [],
  "objection": "The retry repeats the whole request: the transport is given the same question again, and the conversation of the provider starts over with it.  The transcript of the wave 47 puts the work of the run in front of the model, so the model does not have to read the files again, but the tokens of the request are paid for twice, and a provider that is busy for a long time is asked again and again until the budget of the retries is spent.  The budget is small (two by default) and a run that meets a dead provider still ends, where it ended before — the wave buys the runs that meet a provider that dies once and answers the next time, and not the runs that meet a provider that is down.  The wave does not repair the shape of the provider that answers a plan instead of an action (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md): a run that is asked again is asked again by a model that may still only announce its next step. The control of `a-refused-request-is-not-asked-again' makes every failure retryable, and the check fails on two assertions: the model is asked five times after a refusal, and the journal holds the retry of a request that was refused.
