;; The bridge collects what the attached Emacs printed with a process
;; filter.  A process can exit before its last chunk reaches the
;; filter: the answer was then lost and the bridge reported success
;; with an empty output — the person saw an empty buffer that the
;; server had never emptied.
;;
;; The check used to race the subject: it kept a thread spinning to
;; make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached Emacs a
;; hundred and twenty times and failed only when the answer was
;; really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim came out `inconclusive' and the map came out `unknown'.
;; The check now commands the subject instead of racing it.  The
;; hooks it owns hold the answer of the child process until the
;; bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone —
;; the very condition of the defect — and the bridge must deliver
;; the answer all the same.  The same input gives the same verdict
;; every time, and the control of the claim (the drain of the bridge
;; removed) makes the check fail by its own assertion.

;;; Code:

(require 'yeah-bridge)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv \"EMACS\") (file-executable-p (getenv \"EMACS\"))
           (getenv \"EMACS\"))
      (executable-find \"emacs\")
      (expand-file-name \"~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs\"))
  \"The Emacs program that runs the server.\")

(defvar yeah-check--emacsclient
  (let* ((dir (file-name-directory yeah-check--emacs))
         (candidate (expand-file-name \"emacsclient\" dir)))
    (or (and (file-executable-p candidate) candidate)
        (executable-find \"emacsclient\")
        candidate))
  \"The emacsclient program that reaches the server.\")

(defconst yeah-check--answer \"live text\"
  \"The text the attached Emacs holds in the buffer of the check.\")

(defvar yeah-check--hold-the-answer t
  \"Whether the check holds the answer of the child until the bridge drains it.
The control of the claim of the determinism removes this one step: the
check then reads the buffer as it always did, the loss of the answer
is a race again, and the control of the bridge does not bite.\")

(defvar yeah-check--held-chunk nil
  \"The chunk of the child process that the filter has not delivered yet.\")

(defvar yeah-check--held-filter nil
  \"The filter of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.\")

(defvar yeah-check--held-process nil
  \"The process of the bridge, kept to deliver the held chunk later.\")

(defun yeah-check--filter-of (args)
  \"Return the filter of ARGS, or nil when ARGS names none.\"
  (let ((tail args)
        (filter nil))
    (while tail
      (when (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq filter (cadr tail)))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    filter))

(defun yeah-check--without-filter (args)
  \"Return ARGS without the :filter keyword and its value.\"
  (let ((rest nil)
        (tail args))
    (while tail
      (unless (eq (car tail) :filter)
        (setq rest (append rest (list (car tail) (cadr tail)))))
      (setq tail (cddr tail)))
    rest))

(defun yeah-check--around-make-process (orig-fun &rest args)
  \"Create the process of the bridge, but hold what it prints.
The filter of the process keeps the chunk instead of handing it to
the bridge: the answer of the child reaches the bridge only when the
bridge asks for the pending output of a process that is gone.\"
  (let ((filter (yeah-check--filter-of args)))
    (if (and filter yeah-check--hold-the-answer)
        (progn
          (setq yeah-check--held-filter filter)
          (let ((process
                 (apply orig-fun
                        (append (yeah-check--without-filter args)
                                (list :filter
                                      (lambda (_process chunk)
                                        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk
                                              (concat yeah-check--held-chunk
                                                      chunk))))))))

            process))
      (apply orig-fun args))))

  \"Run the event loop of Emacs, and give the held answer to the bridge.
The answer of the child is delivered when the bridge asks for the
pending output of a process that is gone: the bridge reads the answer
of the child after its exit, which is the condition the defect is
about.\"
  (let ((result (apply orig-fun process (or args (list 0.05)))))
    (when (and yeah-check--hold-the-answer
               (null process)
               yeah-check--held-chunk
               yeah-check--held-filter)

        (setq yeah-check--held-chunk nil)
        (funcall yeah-check--held-filter yeah-check--held-process chunk)))
    result))

  \"Advise SYMBOL with FUNCTION.
Emacs 30 asks for the kind of the advice and the older Emacs does
not; the advice itself takes the original function as its first
argument in both.\"
  (if (>= emacs-major-version 30)
      (advice-add symbol :around function)
    (advice-add symbol function)))

(let ((failures nil)
      (name (format \"yeah-bridge-keep-%d\" (random 1000000))))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (make-process
         :name \"yeah-bridge-keep-server\"
         :command (list yeah-check--emacs
                        (concat \"--daemon=\" name)
                        \"--eval\"
                        (format (concat \"(with-current-buffer (get-buffer-create \\\"*yeah-live*\\\") \"
                                        \"(insert \\\"%s\\\"))\")
                                yeah-check--answer))
         :connection-type 'pipe
         :noquery t)

        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) 8)))
          (while (and (< (float-time) deadline)
                      (not (zerop (with-temp-buffer
                                    (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil
                                                  \"-s\" name \"--eval\" \"t\")))))
            (accept-process-output nil 0.1)))
        ;; the hooks of the check: the answer of the child waits for the
        ;; bridge to ask for the pending output of a process that is gone
        (yeah-check--advise 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
        (yeah-check--advise 'accept-process-output
                            #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)
        (unwind-protect
            (let ((text (condition-case err
                           (let ((yeah-bridge-program yeah-check--emacsclient)
                                 (yeah-bridge-server name))
                             (yeah-bridge-buffer-read \"*yeah-live*\"))
                         (error (format \"ERROR: %S\" err)))))
              (unless (equal yeah-check--answer text)
                (push (format \"the bridge lost the answer: it answered %S\" text)
                      failures)))
          (advice-remove 'make-process #'yeah-check--around-make-process)
          (advice-remove 'accept-process-output
                         #'yeah-check--around-accept-process-output)))
    ;; stop the server
    (ignore-errors
      (with-temp-buffer
        (call-process yeah-check--emacsclient nil t nil \"-s\" name \"--eval\" \"(kill-emacs)\")))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message \"bridge-keep: %s\" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

;;; check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el ends here

{
  "id": "wave-47",
  "title": "the model is told what the run has done, and the transcript is a projection of the journal and not a second copy of the run",
  "intent": "The live run of the wave 41 on the code of the wave 46 (2026-11-17, 16:15 and 16:26) made 108 and 122 calls of tools and changed nothing in the repository: the model read `AGENTS.md' again and again, read the plan and the claim of the wave 46 twice, measured a race with experiments of its own in `/tmp', and every answer of the model was a plan ('I'll start by reading the repository rules').  The reason is in the harness and not in the model: every request of the harness starts a fresh conversation with the model.  `yeah-turn--ask' hands the transport a prompt, and the prompt is all the model is told — the messages that came before, the calls the model made, the results it got and its own answers are nowhere in the request, so the model cannot continue the work and begins the task over.  The machinery of the context exists and is not on the road to the model: `yeah-context-project' and `yeah-session-project' compute a projection, the compaction and the pruning write their events into the journal, and the projection itself never reaches a request.  The wave gives the model the transcript of the run: a projection of the journal, the tail of the records of the run, put together when the model is asked and put in front of the prompt.  The transcript names the call the model made, the result it got and the answer it gave, and it ends with the words that keep the work where it is ('Do not start the work over: continue from here.').  The first request of a run carries the request as it is: a run that has done nothing has nothing to tell.  The transcript is a projection and not a second copy of the run: the journal keeps the plain message it was written with, and the projection is put together on the way to the model.  The wave was found by two live runs and not by an offline check, and the check that covers it plays the shape of those runs with a fake transport: no network is touched, but the shape is the one that broke the harness.",
  "touches": [
    "lib/yeah-turn.el",
    "tests/checks/check-the-model-sees-the-run.el",
    "tests/checks/check-wire-control.el",
    "tests/unit/test-yeah-control.el",
    "spec.json",
    "waves/wave-47.json",
    "docs/ARCHITECTURE.md",
    "docs/PLAN.md",
    "docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md",
    "AGENTS.md"
  ],
  "checks": [
    "./scripts/dev byte-compile-all",
    "./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el",
    "./scripts/dev check tests/checks/check-the-model-sees-the-run.el",
    "./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*"
  ],
  "claims": [
    "the-model-is-told-what-the-run-has-done",
    "the-transcript-is-a-projection-and-not-a-second-copy-of-the-run"
  ],
  "commitment": [],
  "objection": "The transcript is a string in the prompt, so the cost of every request of a run grows with the work of the run: the projection is cut at twelve records of the run, and the result of a tool is cut at six hundred characters, so a run of a hundred calls pays for the tail of its own work in every request.  A long run therefore pays for the same work again and again, and the provider is charged for it.  The projection of the context (`lib/yeah-context.el') is the machinery that is meant to answer this, and it is still not on the road to the model: the compaction and the pruning write their events into the journal, but the summary of the work is not what the model is told, and the transcript of the wave is a plain tail of the records.  The wave does not repair the shape of the provider that answers a plan instead of an action (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md): the model is now told what it has done, but a model that keeps announcing its next step is still a model that does not act.  The wave does not repair the defect of the working directory of a session (`cwd' is still not applied to the tools, docs/PLAN.md 17.1).  The wave does not touch the plan of the owner: the waves 41 to 44 keep their numbers and their order, and the runs that found this defect were the runs of the wave 41.",
  "refuted_by": "a request that follows the work of the run carries no trace of the work: neither the call the model made, nor the result it got, nor the answer it gave; or the journal holds the transcript of the run, so that the journal keeps a second copy of the run",
  "note": "Both controls of the wave were run against the code of this wave and bit; each of them made the check fail by an assertion of the check and not by a crash of Emacs.  The control of `the-model-is-told-what-the-run-has-done' takes the transcript out of the request, and the check fails on four assertions: the second request does not carry the transcript of the run, and it names neither the call the model made, nor the result of the call, nor the answer the model gave.  The control of `the-transcript-is-a-projection-and-not-a-second-copy-of-the-run' writes the transcript into the journal, and the check fails on one assertion: the journal holds the transcript, so the projection is a copy of the run.  The check itself was wrong twice before it was right, and both times it was wrong in a way that hid the defect it was written for.  The first version collected the failures with the polarity reversed: `yeah-check--fail' reports a failure when its argument is nil, and the second and third checks handed it the negation of the condition they wanted, so the check reported a failure exactly when the condition held — the check failed on a harness that worked and would have passed on a harness that was broken.  The second version recorded the prompts of the model into the parameter of the fake transport and not into the variable of the caller, so the check saw an empty list of prompts and could not tell a harness that asks the model from a harness that does not.  The two defects of the check were found by reading the check and not by the check: the mechanism of the wave was shown to work by a direct reading of the prompts in an Emacs that printed them, and the check was then read against that reading.  A check that cannot fail is a comment, and a check that fails when the harness is right is worse: it is a comment that reads as a proof.  The wave also changed the code of the unit test of the control (`tests/unit/test-yeah-control.el'), because the prompt of a request now carries the transcript and the test looked for the prompt itself; the test now looks for the prompt by its tail, which is the part the harness does not change.  The wave broke a check of the repository and the map of the method caught it: the check of the control of the wire (`tests/checks/check-wire-control.el') drives a server whose fake model answers the prompt `again' and only that prompt, and it compared the prompt with `(equal prompt \"again\")' -- an exact comparison, which the transcript makes false.  The prompt of the last request of that session therefore never completed, and the check failed on its own assertion.  The fix was in the check and not in the harness: the fake model now matches the prompt by its tail, which is the part the harness does not change.  A wave that changes the shape of the prompt breaks every check that matched the prompt exactly, and the check has to be rewritten: the prompt of a request is not a constant, and the part of it that the harness owns is the tail."
}
{
  "id": "wave-48",
  "title": "a request the provider dropped is asked again, and a request the provider refused is not",
  "intent": "Three live runs of the wave 41 died the same way and for the same reason: the run of 2026-11-17 16:15 with `Curl failed with exit code 28' after 108 calls of tools, the run of 16:26 with `Curl failed with exit code 16' after 122 calls of tools, and the run of 17:10 with `Curl failed with exit code 28' after 70 calls of tools.  The transport to the provider died, the harness took the death of the transport for the end of the run, and the work of the model — hundreds of calls of tools, a plan read over and over — was thrown away with it.  The request never reached an answer: a provider that drops the connection did not refuse the request, and the run said nothing about that difference.  The wave asks such a request again.  The retry is bounded by a budget of its own (`yeah-turn-default-max-retries'), the journal holds the retry as a record of its own (`retry'), and the model is asked the same question with what the run has done in front of it (wave 47), so the retry continues the work instead of starting it over.  A request that the provider refused is not asked again: a refusal is an answer, and the run fails at once and says why.  The status of the wire decides which of the two it is, and the transport of gptel reports that status as a string (`\"529\"', `\"400\"'), so the status is read as a number and not only as a number.  The wave was found by live runs and not by an offline check, and the check that covers it plays the shape of those runs with a fake provider: no network is touched, but the shape is the one that broke the harness, down to the string that carries the status.",
  "touches": [
    "lib/yeah-turn.el",
    "lib/yeah-events.el",
    "tests/checks/check-a-dropped-request-is-asked-again.el",
    "spec.json",
    "waves/wave-48.json",
    "docs/ARCHITECTURE.md",
    "docs/PLAN.md",
    "docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md",
    "AGENTS.md"
  ],
  "checks": [
    "./scripts/dev byte-compile-all",
    "./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/*.el",
    "./scripts/dev check tests/checks/check-a-dropped-request-is-asked-again.el",
    "./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*"
  ],
  "claims": [
    "a-dropped-request-is-asked-again",
    "a-refused-request-is-not-asked-again",
    "the-retries-of-a-run-are-bounded"
  ],
  "commitment": [],
  "objection": "The retry repeats the whole request: the transport is given the same question again, and the conversation of the provider starts over with it.  The transcript of the wave 47 puts the work of the run in front of the model, so the model does not have to read the files again, but the tokens of the request are paid for twice, and a provider that is busy for a long time is asked again and again until the budget of the retries is spent.  The budget is small (two by default) and a run that meets a dead provider still ends, where it ended before — the wave buys the runs that meet a provider that dies once and answers the next time, and not the runs that meet a provider that is down.  The wave does not repair the shape of the provider that answers a plan instead of an action (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md): a run that is asked again is asked again by a model that may still only announce its next step.  The wave does not repair the defect of the working directory of a session (`cwd' is still not applied to the tools, docs/PLAN.md 17.1), and it does not repair the shape of the live runs that read the repository and changed nothing (docs/PLAN.md 17.1: the guard that asks the model for the edit after N calls without a change is still open).  The wave does not touch the plan of the owner: the waves 41 to 44 keep their numbers and their order, and the runs that found this defect were the runs of the wave 41.",
  "refuted_by": "the run ends when the provider dropped the request; or a request the provider refused is asked again; or the retries of a run are not bounded, or the run ends without saying why it stopped",
  "note": "All three controls of the wave were run against the code of this wave and bit; each of them made the check fail by an assertion of the check and not by a crash of Emacs.  The control of `a-dropped-request-is-asked-again' takes the retry out of the harness, and the check fails on twelve assertions: the run does not go on after the dropped request, the model is asked once instead of twice, the retry tells the model nothing, and the retry carries no work of the run.  The control of `a-refused-request-is-not-asked-again' makes every failure retryable, and the check fails on two assertions: the model is asked five times after a refusal, and the journal holds the retry of a request that was refused.  The control of `the-retries-of-a-run-are-bounded' ignores the budget of the retries, and the check fails on four assertions: the model is asked nine times, the journal holds five retries instead of two, the journal holds no error, and the run does not say why it stopped.  The check itself was wrong twice before it was right, and the second of the two defects was a defect of the harness that the check found.  The first version of the fake provider played its script with `pop', which changes the local variable of the caller and not the list itself: the script repeated itself, the harness was asked the same request over and over, and the check measured a harness that never stops -- and the harness under test was a harness that did stop, so the check failed on a harness that worked.  The second version of the fake provider read the status of the wire as a number, which is the shape of no transport: gptel reports the status of the wire as a string (`\"529\"', `\"400\"'), so a check that reads a number cannot tell a busy provider from a provider that refused, and in the live harness a refusal of the provider would have been taken for a request that was never answered and asked again.  The wave found the defect in the harness while it was writing the check of the harness, and the check of the wave plays the real shape of the wire down to the string that carries the status.  The retry does not move the machine of the states: the run was waiting for the model and waits again, so the counter of the twenty transitions of `lib/yeah-loop.el' is untouched, and a check that counts the states of a run sees the same states it saw before the wave.  The record of the retry is a record of the journal and not a line of the transcript of the model: the transcript names it in one line (`[retry] the provider dropped the request: ...'), and the journal keeps the reason the retry was made."
}

service.
- The method `session/set_mode` does not exist: the permission profile of a
  session cannot be changed over the wire, and a client that asks is answered
  with `-32601`.
- The model of a session cannot be changed over the wire: neither
  `session/set_model` nor `session/set_config_option` exists, so an
  orchestrator cannot choose the model of a run.
- The `mcpServers` of a session are ignored: the tools of an MCP server that a
  client names do not reach the model.
- The `tool_call` of the wire names the tool and carries what it was called
  with and what it returned (`rawInput` and `rawOutput`), but no `kind`: a
  client that renders the call of a tool by its kind — a read, an edit, a
  shell — sees the name of the tool and nothing else.  The arguments of a
  call are positional, so a client that looks for named fields (`path`,
  `oldText`, `query`) does not find them.
- The process of the server outlives the agent.  A client that keeps the pipe
  of the server open after the last turn leaves an Emacs process alive, and
  some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace: one
  of them was measured with 1.9 million involuntary context switches and six
  voluntary ones, and it never slept.  The read loop of the server is not the
  cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
  and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
  per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request
  of the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet.  The client that
  leaves the process behind is the plugin that spawned it: nothing closes the
  pipe of the server when the session of the agent is over.

**The measurement.**

- The pilot is three tasks.  The sample is small, and the numbers of the runs
  of waves 33, 34, 35, 36, 37 and 38 (2 of 3, 1 of 3, 2 of 3 and one blocked,
  2 of 3, 2 of 3) differ by the noise of the provider and of the model.
- The second harness is `pi` 1.1.0, which is checked in the environment;
  `opencode` is not installed here.
- One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The check of
  `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a hundred
  and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails only
  when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence bound that claim
  on 2026-11-16: five bit, and one did not — the control reached the
  subject, the verifier after the control still passed, the claim came out
  `inconclusive`, and the map came out `unknown`.  A claim whose control does
  not always bite is not established: until the check of that race is
  deterministic, the verdict of the map can be `unknown` for a reason that has
  nothing to do with the code it names.  The claim itself is not weakened
  here, and nobody may quote it as established on the strength of the runs
  where the race happened.

### 17.2 The decisions of the owner

None of these may be decided by an agent.  Each of them is recorded with
`mathc record` when a person decides it, and not by an edit of the code.

**One of them was decided on 2026-11-16 (az): the priority of the next wave.**
It is recorded as the judgment claim
`the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves` — a human review, bound to
the materials of this repository by `mathc record` — and the plan that the
decision refers to is §18.  The decisions that §18.5 names stay open: no
wave of that plan takes them, and no agent may take them either.

- The threshold of the parity, and the final set of the tasks of the benchmark
  (`docs/PLAN.md` §13).  Until the threshold is decided, the parity is not
  claimed anywhere, and the pilot stays a measurement.  **Open** (§18.5).
- Whether a run that the provider silenced is a failure of the agent or a run
  that was never measured.  The runner of the benchmark knows a run that the
  provider failed from the error records of the journal; the silence of the
  provider is not an error record, so such a run counts against the agent
  today.  The decision changes the number of every pilot, and the pilot of
  wave 36 measured a task of Yeah in that shape (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The
  live checks and the pilot after wave 36").  **Open** (§18.5).
- The second harness of the comparison, if it is not `pi`.
- The placement of the frame server for the pixel check.  The check is outside
  the map of the method: without a frame server it is blocked, and not a pass.
- The priority of the next wave: the parallel children of Stage 7, a wider
  pilot, a real editor against a live provider, or the gaps of the service
  path.  **Decided on 2026-11-16 (az):** the order is wave 41 (the
  deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the process of the server),
  wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave 44 (parallel
  children in a live turn) — §18, recorded as the judgment claim
  `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves`.
- The minimum versions of Emacs and gptel, and the cycle of the releases.
- The policy of the unattended command and of the network.
- Whether a restricted evaluation deserves a design of its own process at all.
- The access of the service to the personal buffers of the person.
- The channels of the distribution and the signing of the packages.
- The compatibility with Apache-2.0 of every optional integration.
- The budget of the completion supervision of a child of a delegation.  The
  default of the kernel is positive since wave 39, and the default of the child
  is still zero: a child that only talks and never calls `finish` ends as a
  completed child today.  The wave did not change the default of the child,
  because the claims of the delegation (§17.1) do not say that a child that
  never finishes is a failed child, and a silent change of that meaning would
  make the claims of wave 35–37 untrue.  **Open** (§18.5).

### 17.3 The order, if the owner says nothing

The owner did say something about the next waves on 2026-11-16 (az), and that
order (§18) comes first.  What follows is the order of the rest, if the
owner says nothing about them either.

1. **The pilot again**, with a larger set of tasks, when the provider answers.
   The row of a run that did not finish names the shape of it since wave 38,
   so a reader of the pilot sees the cause of a failed check and not only its
   verdict.  Whether such a run is a failure of the agent or a run that was
   never measured is still the decision of the owner (§17.2), because it
   changes the number of every pilot.
2. **The pixel check**, when the owner names the place of the frame server.

Wave 38 closed the naming of the shape: the reason of the row of a run that
did not finish says what the journal of the run holds, and the verdict of the
row is not touched by that.

Wave 37 closed the depth of the tree: the children of a run and their depth are
in the journal now, and a restart of the harness finds the child of a run again
and tells what became of it.

Wave 36 was the plan above that said otherwise: it was to be the parallel
children of the delegation, and the audit proved that several children in one
turn of the parent work already.  Wave 36 was the defect that the audit found
instead — the delegation was written into the journal of another run — and with
it the short id of the child and the time of the child.

Re-opened when a person says so: the math-coding aim block in AGENTS.md is
written by `mathc install` and is not edited by hand.

## 18. The plan of the next waves

The owner named the order of the next waves on 2026-11-16 (az), after the
report on the readiness of Yeah for self-development and after the
integration with the orchestrator Paseo.  The decision is recorded by the
method as the judgment claim `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves`
(a human review, not a machine verifier), and this section is the plan that
the decision refers to.  The order is by the price of the defect: the wave
that makes the verdict of the method unreadable goes first, and the wave that
opens the path from a model to a working program goes last.

The order of the next waves, named by the owner on 2026-11-16: **wave 41, wave 42, wave 43, wave 44.**

They are: wave 41 (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the
process of the server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave
44 (parallel children in a live turn).

One wave was executed before them: **wave 45** (2026-11-17), the repair of
the harness that the live test of the harness forced — a tool that returns
bytes that are not text took the whole Emacs process down, and the four
waves of this plan need a harness that lives to carry them (§16.24).  The
order named by the owner is unchanged: wave 41 is still the first of the
four.

Every wave below names the defect it removes, the claims it registers, the
control that has to bite, and the criteria that close it.  A wave that ends
without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

**What is known and what is not.**  The read loop of the server is not the
cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request of
the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet: `ptrace` and `strace`
are not available in this environment ("Operation not permitted"), so the
localization has to be done by measurement — the ticks of `/proc/<pid>/stat`,
not the percentage of the CPU that `top` prints.

**What changes.**
1. *The life cycle.*  The server has a way to end that does not depend on the
   client closing the pipe: the session ends, and the process exits.  The
   plugin of Paseo (`yeah-provider`, outside this repository) closes the pipe
   of the server when the session of the agent is over; the kernel side gives
   it a way to say so.
2. *The spin.*  The loop on the path of the live request is localized by
   instrumentation — a counter of the iterations of the pump and of the
   request of the provider — measured the way the defect itself was measured.
   The loop that spins is then removed, and the bound becomes a check.

payload:
- The process of the server outlives the agent.  A client that keeps the pipe
  of the server open after the last turn leaves an Emacs process alive, and
  some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace: one
  of them was measured with 1.9 million involuntary context switches and six
  voluntary ones, and it never slept.  The read loop of the server is not the
  cause: an idle server costs no CPU and leaves cleanly when its input ends,
  and a server that waits for a turn the model never answers costs about four
  per cent of a core.  The spin is therefore on the path of the live request
  of the provider, and the loop itself is not localized yet.  The client that
  leaves the process behind is the plugin that spawned it: nothing closes the
  pipe of the server when the session of the agent is over.

**The measurement.**

- The pilot is three tasks.  The sample is small, and the numbers of the runs
  of waves 33, 34, 35, 36, 37 and 38 (2 of 3, 1 of 3, 2 of 3 and one blocked,
  2 of 3, 2 of 3) differ by the noise of the provider and of the model.
- The second harness is `pi` 1.1.0, which is checked in the environment;
  `opencode` is not installed here.
- One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The check of
  `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a hundred
  and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails only
  when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence bound that claim
  on 2026-11-16: five bit, and one did not — the control reached the
  subject, the verifier after the control still passed, the claim came out
  `inconclusive`, and the map came out `unknown`.  A claim whose control does
  not always bite is not established: until the check of that race is
  deterministic, the verdict of the map can be `unknown` for a reason that has
  nothing to do with the code it names.  The claim itself is not weakened
  here, and nobody may quote it as established on the strength of the runs
  where the race happened.

### 17.2 The decisions of the owner

None of these may be decided by an agent.  Each of them is recorded with
`mathc record` when a person decides it, and not by an edit of the code.

**One of them was decided on 2026-11-16 (az): the priority of the next wave.**
It is recorded as the judgment claim
`the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves` — a human review, bound to
the materials of this repository by `mathc record` — and the plan that the
decision refers to is §18.  The decisions that §18.5 names stay open: no
wave of that plan takes them, and no agent may take them either.

- The threshold of the parity, and the final set of the tasks of the benchmark
  (`docs/PLAN.md` §13).  Until the threshold is decided, the parity is not
  claimed anywhere, and the pilot stays a measurement.  **Open** (§18.5).
- Whether a run that the provider silenced is a failure of the agent or a run
  that was never measured.  The runner of the benchmark knows a run that the
  provider failed from the error records of the journal; the silence of the
  provider is not an error record, so such a run counts against the agent
  today.  The decision changes the number of every pilot, and the pilot of
  wave 36 measured a task of Yeah in that shape (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, "The
  live checks and the pilot after wave 36").  **Open** (§18.5).
- The second harness of the comparison, if it is not `pi`.
- The placement of the frame server for the pixel check.  The check is outside
  the map of the method: without a frame server it is blocked, and not a pass.
- The priority of the next wave: the parallel children of Stage 7, a wider
  pilot, a real editor against a live provider, or the gaps of the service
  path.  **Decided on 2026-11-16 (az):** the order is wave 41 (the
  deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the process of the server),
  wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave 44 (parallel
  children in a live turn) — §18, recorded as the judgment claim
  `the-owner-decided-the-order-of-the-next-waves`.
- The minimum versions of Emacs and gptel, and the cycle of the releases.
- The policy of the unattended command and of the network.
- Whether a restricted evaluation deserves a design of its own process at all.
- The access of the service to the personal buffers of the person.
- The channels of the distribution and the signing of the packages.
- The compatibility with Apache-2.0 of every optional integration.

payload:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}

(a human review, not a machine verifier), and this section is the plan that
the decision refers to.  The order is by the price of the defect: the wave
that makes the verdict of the method unreadable goes first, and the wave that
opens the path from a model to a working program goes last.

The order of the next waves, named by the owner on 2026-11-16: **wave 41, wave 42, wave 43, wave 44.**

They are: wave 41 (the deterministic verifier of the bridge), wave 42 (the
process of the server), wave 43 (the surface of ACP for an orchestrator), wave
44 (parallel children in a live turn).

One wave was executed before them: **wave 45** (2026-11-17), the repair of
the harness that the live test of the harness forced — a tool that returns
bytes that are not text took the whole Emacs process down, and the four
waves of this plan need a harness that lives to carry them (§16.24).  The
order named by the owner is unchanged: wave 41 is still the first of the
four.

Every wave below names the defect it removes, the claims it registers, the
control that has to bite, and the criteria that close it.  A wave that ends
without a control that bites is not a wave: it is a change of the code with
no evidence.

### 18.1 Wave 41 — the verifier of the bridge decides the race by construction

**The defect.**  One verifier of the standing specification is a race.  The
check of `bridge-keeps-the-answer` reads the buffer of an attached Emacs a
hundred and twenty times while a thread keeps the parent late, and it fails
only when the answer is really lost.  Six runs of the evidence on 2026-11-16:
five bit, one did not — the control reached the subject, the verifier after
the control still passed, the claim came out `inconclusive`, and the map came
out `unknown`.  The code was not the cause of that verdict; the evidence was.

**Why this wave is first.**  Every other wave of this plan ends with a run
of the method, and a run whose verdict depends on a race may say `unknown`
for a reason that has nothing to do with the code it names.  A map that says
`unknown` because of a race cannot be read.

**What changes.**  The check stops racing the subject and starts commanding
it: the loss of the answer becomes a condition that the check arranges — a
barrier the parent waits for, a hook the check owns — so that the same
input gives the same verdict every time.  The control of the claim becomes
the same arrangement with one step removed, and the check must then fail by
its own assertion.

**The claims.**
- `bridge-keeps-the-answer` — the existing claim, re-bound with a control
  that bites every time (register `fact`, requirement: the check of the
  bridge).
- `the-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction` — a new claim: the
  check of the bridge gives the same verdict on ten consecutive runs of the
  control, and the control bites on each of them (register `fact`).

**The exit criteria.**
1. Ten consecutive runs of the control bite: every one of them fails by an
   assertion of the check, not by a crash of Emacs and not by a timeout.
2. Two consecutive runs of the method end in `green`, with no `inconclusive`
   claim and no `unknown` verdict.

**The estimate.**  Half a day to a day.  **What this wave does not fix.**  It
repairs the evidence, not the harness: nothing of the run itself changes.

### 18.2 Wave 42 — the server does not outlive the agent, and it does not spin

**The defect.**  Two defects of one life cycle.  The process of the ACP
server outlives the agent: a client that keeps the pipe of the server open
after the last turn leaves an Emacs process behind, and nothing closes it.
And some of those processes burn half a core in a tight loop of userspace:
one of them was measured with 1,921,354 involuntary context switches and six
voluntary ones — it never slept — at 25–60 % of a core.

(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv \"EMACS\") (file-executable-p (getenv \"EMACS\"))
           (getenv \"EMACS\"))
      (executable-find \"emacs\")
      (expand-file-name \"~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs\"))
  \"The Emacs program that runs the check of the bridge.\")

(defvar yeah-check--root
  (let ((file (or load-file-name buffer-file-name default-directory)))
    (file-name-directory
     (directory-file-name
      (directory-file-name
       (directory-file-name (file-name-directory file))))))
  \"The root of the repository.\")

(defvar yeah-check--runs 10
  \"How many consecutive runs of the control the claim of the bridge asks for.\")

(defvar yeah-check--run-timeout 120
  \"Seconds a run of the check of the bridge may take.\")

(defconst yeah-check--bridge-check \"tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el\"
  \"The check of the bridge, the one this check runs.\")

(defun yeah-check--control-of (claim-id)
  \"Return the control of the claim CLAIM-ID, or nil when it has none.
The control is read from the standing specification: the check runs
the control that the claim declares, and not a copy of it.\"
  (let* ((spec (json-read-file (expand-file-name \"spec.json\" yeah-check--root)))
         (claims (alist-get \"claims\" spec))
         (claim (seq-find (lambda (entry) (equal (alist-get \"id\" entry) claim-id))
                           claims)))
    (and claim (alist-get \"control\" claim))))

(defun yeah-check--copy-tree (source target)
  \"Copy the tree of the directory SOURCE into the directory TARGET.\"
  (make-directory target t)
  (dolist (entry (directory-files source t directory-files-no-dot-files-regexp t))
    (let ((name (file-name-nondirectory entry)))
      (if (file-directory-p entry)
          (yeah-check--copy-tree entry (expand-file-name name target))
        (file-copy-file entry (expand-file-name name target))))))

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  \"Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.
Return the code of the run and the words it printed.  The code of a
run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'.\"
  (let ((output \"\")
        (words (generate-new-buffer \" *yeah-bridge-check words*\"))
        (process (make-process
                  :name \"yeah-bridge-check-run\"
                  :command (list yeah-check--emacs \"-Q\" \"--batch\"
                                 \"-L\" \"lib\" \"-L\" \".\"
                                 \"-l\" yeah-check--bridge-check)
                  :directory directory
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                  :environment (cons (concat \"EMACS=\" yeah-check--emacs)
                                     process-environment)
                  :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                            (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                  :stderr words)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))
          (while (and (process-live-p process)
                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (if (process-live-p process)
              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  \"Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code.\"
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name \"yeah-bridge-control\"
                  :command (list \"sh\" \"-c\" control)
                  :directory directory
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))

(let ((failures nil)
      (control (yeah-check--control-of \"bridge-keeps-the-answer\"))
      (directory (make-temp-file \"yeah-bridge-control-\" t)))
  (unwind-protect
      (progn
        (if (null control)
            (push \"the claim of the bridge declares no control to run\" failures)
          ;; the copy of the repository the control breaks
          (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name \"lib\" yeah-check--root)
                                 (expand-file-name \"lib\" directory))
          (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name \"tests\" yeah-check--root)
                                 (expand-file-name \"tests\" directory))
          ;; the check of the bridge passes on the whole bridge
          (let ((run (yeah-check--run-bridge-check yeah-check--root)))
            (unless (eq (car run) 0)
              (push (format \"the check of the bridge does not pass on the whole bridge: %S\"
                            (car run))
                    failures)))
          ;; the control of the claim, and ten runs of the check against it
          (let ((code (yeah-check--apply-control control directory)))
            (unless (eq code 0)
              (push (format \"the control of the claim of the bridge did not apply: %S\" code)
                    failures)))
          (dotimes (run yeah-check--runs)
            (let* ((result (yeah-check--run-bridge-check directory))
                   (code (car result))
                   (words (cdr result)))
              (cond
               ((eq code 'timeout)
                (push (format \"the run %d of the control did not finish in %d seconds\"
                              (1+ run) yeah-check--run-timeout)
                      failures))
               ((not (eq code 1))
                (push (format \"the run %d of the control ended with the code %S: the control did not bite by an assertion\"
                              (1+ run) code)
                      failures))
               ((not (string-match-p \"bridge-keep:\" words))
                (push (format \"the run %d of the control did not fail by an assertion of the check: %S\"
                              (1+ run) words)
                      failures))))))
    (when (file-directory-p directory)
      (delete-directory directory t))
    (dolist (failure failures)
      (message \"bridge-race: %s\" failure))
    (if failures
        (kill-emacs 1)
      (kill-emacs 0))))

("tests/checks/check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el" ";;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el --- the check of the bridge decides the race by construction -*- lexical-binding: t; no-byte-compile: t -*-
;;
;; Copyright (C) 2026  Petr Kosov
;;
;; This file is part of Yeah.
;;
;; Yeah is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under
;; the terms of the Apache License, Version 2.0.

;;; Commentary:
;;
;; The check of the bridge used to race the subject: it kept a thread
;; spinning to make the parent late, read the buffer of the attached
;; Emacs a hundred and twenty times, and failed only when the answer
;; was really lost.  Five runs of six bit and one did not (2026-11-16):
;; the claim of the bridge came out `inconclusive' and the map came
;; out `unknown'.  An evidence that decides its verdict by a race
;; cannot be read.
;;
;; This check is the evidence of that repair.  It takes the control of
;; the claim of the bridge — the drain of the bridge removed — and runs
;; the check of the bridge against it ten times in a copy of the
;; repository.  Every one of the ten runs must fail by an assertion of
;; the check: the same code, the same verdict, ten times in a row.  A
;; run that crashes Emacs, a run that hangs and a run that passes are
;; all failures of this check.
;;
;; The check of the bridge must also pass on the whole bridge, before
;; the control is applied: a check that fails whatever the subject does
;; proves nothing.

;;; Code:

(require 'json)
(require 'seq)

(defvar yeah-check--emacs
  (or (and (getenv \"EMACS\") (file-executable-p (getenv \"EMACS\"))
           (getenv \"EMACS\"))
      (executable-find \"emacs\")
      (expand-file-name \"~/.nix-profile/bin/emacs\"))
  \"The Emacs program that runs the check of the bridge.\")

(defvar yeah-check--root
  (let ((file (or load-file-name buffer-file-name default-directory)))
    (file-name-directory
     (directory-file-name
      (directory-file-name
       (directory-file-name (file-name-directory file))))))
  \"The root of the repository.\")

(defvar yeah-check--runs 10
  \"How many consecutive runs of the control the claim of the bridge asks for.\")

(defvar yeah-check--run-timeout 120
  \"Seconds a run of the check of the bridge may take.\")

(defconst yeah-check--bridge-check \"tests/checks/check-bridge-keeps-the-answer.el\"
  \"The check of the bridge, the one this check runs.\")

(defun yeah-check--control-of (claim-id)
  \"Return the control of the claim CLAIM-ID, or nil when it has none.
The control is read from the standing specification: the check runs
the control that the claim declares, and not a copy of it.\"
  (let* ((spec (json-read-file (expand-file-name \"spec.json\" yeah-check--root)))
         (claims (alist-get \"claims\" spec))
         (claim (seq-find (lambda (entry) (equal (alist-get \"id\" entry) claim-id))
                           claims)))
    (and claim (alist-get \"control\" claim))))

(defun yeah-check--copy-tree (source target)
  \"Copy the tree of the directory SOURCE into the directory TARGET.\"
  (make-directory target t)
  (dolist (entry (directory-files source t directory-files-no-dot-files-regexp t))
    (let ((name (file-name-nondirectory entry)))
      (if (file-directory-p entry)
          (yeah-check--copy-tree entry (expand-file-name name target))
        (file-copy-file entry (expand-file-name name target))))))

(defun yeah-check--bridge-command (directory)
  \"Return the command that runs the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.\"
  (list yeah-check--emacs \"-Q\" \"--batch\"
        \"-L\" (expand-file-name \"lib\" directory)
        \"-L\" directory
        \"-l\" (expand-file-name yeah-check--bridge-check directory)))

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  \"Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.
Return the code of the run and the words it printed.  The code of a
run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'.\"
  (let ((output \"\")
        (words (generate-new-buffer \" *yeah-bridge-check words*\"))
        (process (make-process
                  :name \"yeah-bridge-check-run\"
                  :command (yeah-check--bridge-command directory)
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                  :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                            (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                  :stderr words)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))
          (while (and (process-live-p process)
                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (if (process-live-p process)
              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  \"Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code.\"
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name \"yeah-bridge-control\"
                  :command (list \"sh\" \"-c\"
                                 (format \"cd %s && %s\"
                                         (shell-quote-argument directory)
                                         control))
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))

(defun yeah-check--failures ()
  \"Run the check of the bridge against the control of the claim.
Return the list of the failures of the check.\"
  (let ((failures nil)
        (control (yeah-check--control-of \"bridge-keeps-the-answer\"))
        (directory (make-temp-file \"yeah-bridge-control-\" t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (if (null control)
              (push \"the claim of the bridge declares no control to run\" failures)
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name \"lib\" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name \"lib\" directory))
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name \"tests\" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name \"tests\" directory))
            ;; the check of the bridge passes on the whole bridge
            (let ((run (yeah-check--run-bridge-check yeah-check--root)))
              (unless (eq (car run) 0)
                (push (format \"the check of the bridge does not pass on the whole bridge: %S\"
                              (car run))
                      failures)))
            ;; the control of the claim, and ten runs of the check against it
            (let ((code (yeah-check--apply-control control directory)))
              (unless (eq code 0)
                (push (format \"the control of the claim of the bridge did not apply: %S\"
                              code)
                      failures)))
            (dotimes (run yeah-check--runs)
              (let* ((result (yeah-check--run-bridge-check directory))
                     (code (car result))
                     (words (cdr result)))
                (cond
                 ((eq code 'timeout)
                  (push (format \"the run %d of the control did not finish in %d seconds\"
                                (1+ run) yeah-check--run-timeout)
                        failures))
                 ((not (eq code 1))
                  (push (format \"the run %d of the control ended with the code %S: the control did not bite by an assertion\"
                                (1+ run) code)
                        failures))
                 ((not (string-match-p \"bridge-keep:\" words))
                  (push (format \"the run %d of the control did not fail by an assertion of the check: %S\"
                                (1+ run) words)
                        failures)))))))
      (when (file-directory-p directory)
        (delete-directory directory t)))
    failures))

(let ((failures (yeah-check--failures)))
  (dolist (failure failures)
    (message \"bridge-race: %s\" failure))
  (if failures
      (kill-emacs 1)
    (kill-emacs 0)))

;;; check-bridge-check-decides-the-race-by-construction.el ends here
" t nil)

        (file-copy-file entry (expand-file-name name target))))))

(defun yeah-check--bridge-command (directory)
  "Return the command that runs the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY."
  (list yeah-check--emacs "-Q" "--batch"
        "-L" (expand-file-name "lib" directory)
        "-L" directory
        "-l" (expand-file-name yeah-check--bridge-check directory)))

(defun yeah-check--run-bridge-check (directory)
  "Run the check of the bridge in DIRECTORY.
Return the code of the run and the words it printed.  The code of a
run that did not finish in time is the symbol `timeout'."
  (let ((output "")
        (words (generate-new-buffer " *yeah-bridge-check words*"))
        (process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-check-run"
                  :command (yeah-check--bridge-command directory)
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8)
                  :filter (lambda (_process chunk)
                            (setq output (concat output chunk)))
                  :stderr words)))
    (unwind-protect
        (let ((deadline (+ (float-time) yeah-check--run-timeout)))
          (while (and (process-live-p process)
                      (< (float-time) deadline))
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (if (process-live-p process)
              (progn
                (ignore-errors (kill-process process))
                (cons 'timeout output))
            (cons (process-exit-status process)
                  (concat output (with-current-buffer words (buffer-string))))))
      (when (buffer-live-p words)
        (kill-buffer words)))))

(defun yeah-check--apply-control (control directory)
  "Run the shell command CONTROL in DIRECTORY and return its code."
  (let ((process (make-process
                  :name "yeah-bridge-control"
                  :command (list "sh" "-c"
                                 (format "cd %s && %s"
                                         (shell-quote-argument directory)
                                         control))
                  :connection-type 'pipe
                  :noquery t
                  :coding '(utf-8 . utf-8))))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (while (process-live-p process)
            (accept-process-output process 0.1))
          (process-exit-status process))
      (when (process-live-p process)
        (ignore-errors (kill-process process))))))

(defun yeah-check--failures ()
  "Run the check of the bridge against the control of the claim.
Return the list of the failures of the check."
  (let ((failures nil)
        (control (yeah-check--control-of "bridge-keeps-the-answer"))
        (directory (make-temp-file "yeah-bridge-control-" t)))
    (unwind-protect
        (progn
          (if (null control)
              (push "the claim of the bridge declares no control to run" failures)
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "lib" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "lib" directory))
            (yeah-check--copy-tree (expand-file-name "tests" yeah-check--root)
                                   (expand-file-name "tests" directory))
            ;; the check of the bridge passes on the whole bridge
            (let ((run (yeah-check--run-bridge-check yeah-check--root)))
              (unless (eq (car run) 0)
                (push (format "the check of the bridge does not pass on the whole bridge: %S"
                              (car run))
                      failures)))
            ;; the control of the claim, and ten runs of the check against it
            (let ((code (yeah-check--apply-control control directory)))
              (unless (eq code 0)
                (push (format "the control of the claim of the bridge did not apply: %S"
                              code)
                      failures)))
            (dotimes (run yeah-check--runs)
              (let* ((result (yeah-check--run-bridge-check directory))
                     (code (car result))
                     (words (cdr result)))
                (cond
                 ((eq code 'timeout)
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not finish in %d seconds"
                                (1+ run) yeah-check--run-timeout)
                        failures))
                 ((not (eq code 1))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control ended with the code %S: the control did not bite by an assertion"
                                (1+ run) code)
                        failures))
                 ((not (string-match-p "bridge-keep:" words))
                  (push (format "the run %d of the control did not fail by an assertion of the check: %S"
                                (1+ run) words)
                        failures)))))))
      (when (file-directory-p directory)
        (delete-directory directory t)))
    failures))

(let ((failures (yeah-check--failures)))
  (dolist (failure failures)
    (message "bridge-race: %s" failure))
  (if failures
      (kill-emacs 1)
    (kill-emacs 0)))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/dev — Yeah development wrapper.
#
# Subcommands:
#   smoke                 — print "yeah-dev ok" and exit 0
#   byte-compile-all      — byte-compile every file under lib/ and the package entry
#   ert FILE...           — run ERT test files (tests/unit/*.el)
#   bench [--run]         — validate the benchmark task set, or run the benchmark
#   pixel                 — photograph the real interface and compare two pictures
#   map                   — the standing specification: claims, states, uncovered
#   run                   — execute the checks, bind the evidence, write the trail
#   gate                  — run, then map; the exit code is the verdict
#   help                  — this text
#
# Exit codes (the method's scale, A13/A14):
#   0 — pass       (Green)
#   1 — fail       (Red)
#   2 — blocked    (input error: bad arguments, unknown subcommand)
#   3 — unknown    (the method could not tell: a tool is missing, a check
#                    did not run, a control did not bite)
#
# The method binary is `mathc`: set MATHC to its path, or put it on PATH.
# It comes from the math-coding repository (`nix build` there writes
# ./result/bin/mathc). The method's own files — spec.json and waves/ — are
# part of this project, not of the tool.

set -u

cmd="${1:-help}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift

find_emacs() {
  if [ -n "${EMACS:-}" ] && [ -x "${EMACS}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${EMACS}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v emacs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v emacs
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.nix-profile/bin/emacs"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

find_mathc() {
  if [ -n "${MATHC:-}" ]; then
    printf '%s' "${MATHC}"
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v mathc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    command -v mathc
    return 0
  fi
  if [ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$HOME/.local/bin/mathc"
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

need_mathc() {
  mathc_bin="$(find_mathc)" || {
    echo "scripts/dev $cmd: mathc is not on PATH and MATHC is not set." >&2
    echo "  Get it from the math-coding repository: nix build  (it writes result/bin/mathc)." >&2
    exit 3
  }
}

# Emacs loads a byte-compiled file when it exists, even when the source is
# newer ("Source file ... newer than byte-compiled file; using older file").
# A stale .elc next to a modified source therefore makes every check test
# yesterday's code instead of today's. The bytecode is a build artifact, not
# a part of the tree: it is removed before anything is loaded.
clean_bytecode() {
  rm -f lib/*.elc bench/*.elc
}
